answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by charging every identity a real, slashable cost: before trading, an agent locks a small deposit and signs its work history with a unique cipher key. Other agents read that history like light through a prism - one key, one verifiable record - so a fake cannot borrow a reputable agent's past. Spinning up a thousand Sybils then means funding a thousand deposits and building a thousand histories, while an honest agent pays once. The deposit is the copper floor: cheap to join, ruinous to fake at scale, and forfeited on proven fraud.
